data.summary: The `src` directory is the Rust backend core of an axum-based 'AIO-style' dev sandbox server. It contains the application entry point (main.rs), the data-driven service/button registry and manifest builder (config.rs), the shared application state (state.rs), the websocket terminal pty bridge (pty.rs), and the background model-config sync task from sandbox-mgr (mgr_sync.rs). Together these files wire up the HTTP router, static SPA serving, dynamic service manifest API, terminal session bridging, and configuration synchronization.

file_insights.name: main.rs
file_insights.summary: Application entry point that builds the axum router, wires shared state, serves the static SPA, and spawns background tasks.
file_insights.source_summary: Defines a single async `main` function using tokio and axum. It documents Phase B/E features (data-driven service manifest, terminal WebSocket bridge via terminal.rs + pty.rs) and sets up static file serving plus the HTTP/WebSocket surface for the sandbox.
file_insights.detailed_description: main.rs is the binary entry point of the server: it initializes AppState, mounts the /api (manifest, models, terminal ws), /v1 and /mcp route seams, serves the built SPA via ServeDir, and starts the mgr_sync background task. It is the composition root that pulls together config, state, pty, routes and mgr_sync modules.
responsibilities: Initialize shared AppState at startup
Compose and launch the axum router with /api, /v1, /mcp seams
Serve the static frontend build via ServeDir
Spawn background tasks such as mgr_sync

file_insights.name: config.rs
file_insights.summary: Service registry and manifest builder that merges compile-time built-in services with runtime user-registered buttons and resolves executable paths.
file_insights.source_summary: Defines structs ServicesFile, ButtonsFile, ButtonDef, Service, ServiceType, ManifestEntry, Manifest and PathCache, plus functions load_services, load_buttons, parse_button_defs, merge_services, build_manifest, resolve_path_dirs, resolve_login_path, expand_one and humanize_id. Uses include_str! for the baked-in services.toml and supports async, TTL-cached PATH resolution.
file_insights.detailed_description: config.rs is the largest module (810 lines, 42 functions) and implements the data-driven service model: it parses services.toml baked into the binary and /root/.aio/buttons.toml from the persistent workspace volume, merges them, and builds a manifest consumed by the frontend. It also resolves PATH/login-shell directories with caching and expands command tokens, forming the core business logic for discovering what buttons/agents a sandbox exposes.
responsibilities: Parse baked-in services.toml and runtime buttons.toml into Service records
Merge built-in and user services with override semantics
Resolve login-shell PATH directories with an async TTL cache
Expand command tokens and humanize service IDs
Build the Manifest served to the frontend

file_insights.name: mgr_sync.rs
file_insights.summary: Background task that polls sandbox-mgr for the assigned model config and agent subset, diffing and rendering it into the local store.
file_insights.source_summary: Defines SyncPayload and Fetched types, spawn_mgr_sync, agent_name, sync_url, fetch, urlencode, temp_dir, sample_config and config_json_equal. Tests validate config diffing, sync URL construction, payload decoding and per-agent subset rendering behavior.
file_insights.detailed_description: mgr_sync.rs implements the Phase 4b/D8 config pull: when MGR_URL is set, it periodically (every 60s plus at startup) GETs /api/models/sync?name=<sandbox> to fetch the sandbox's assigned profile/agents, diffs against the current config, and writes/renders the canonical model config via apply_selected_agents. It includes substantial unit tests covering diffing, wire-shape decoding and subset rendering.
responsibilities: Spawn and drive the periodic 60s mgr config pull loop
Fetch and decode the mgr sync wire payload for this sandbox
Diff remote canonical config against local state
Write the model store and render assigned agent subsets
Provide unit tests for diff/render/URL behavior

file_insights.name: state.rs
file_insights.summary: Defines AppState, the shared immutable-plus-locked context passed to all axum handlers.
file_insights.source_summary: Declares the AppState struct and its implementation (constructor/accessors), storing builtin services, the buttons file path, models file path, PathCache and StatsSnapshot behind Arc/Mutex. It documents env-driven paths such as AIO_BUTTONS_FILE and AIO_MODELS_FILE.
file_insights.detailed_description: state.rs holds AppState, which bundles the parsed built-in services, file paths for runtime buttons.toml and the canonical models file, a PathCache, and a stats snapshot behind synchronization primitives. It is built once at startup and shared via axum::State, acting as the central dependency-injection context for route handlers.
responsibilities: Hold immutable built-in service registry
Expose paths to runtime buttons/models config files
Provide shared PathCache and StatsSnapshot behind locks
Serve as the axum State context for handlers

file_insights.name: pty.rs
file_insights.summary: Portable-pty bridge that spawns a login shell (or a command under it) and returns reader/writer/child handles for the terminal WebSocket.
file_insights.source_summary: Defines the PtySession struct and the spawn_pty function that creates a pty pair via native_pty_system, inherits the root environment (so /usr/local/bin such as opencode is on PATH), and returns io::Result<PtySession>.
file_insights.detailed_description: pty.rs wraps portable-pty to spawn a login shell as root with HOME=/root and TERM=xterm-256color, optionally running a ?cmd= under it, in a given cwd. It returns a PtySession with the read/write ends and child process handle, which the terminal WebSocket route bridges to xterm.js.
responsibilities: Create a portable-pty session pair
Spawn a login shell as root with the inherited environment
Support optional ?cmd= execution under the login shell
Return reader/writer/child handles for the WS bridge
